abstract.para: The agama command-line program lets you inspect or change the installation settings, handle installation profiles, start the installation, and monitor its progress. This reference lists every agama command and subcommand.

section.title: Global options
section.para: These options apply to the agama command itself, before any subcommand:

listitem.para: URI pointing to &agama;'s remote host. For example, https://my-server.lan, my-server.local, or localhost:10443. Defaults to http://localhost.
Whether to accept invalid (for example, self-signed) certificates. Defaults to false.
Some commands can work even without a connection to the &agama; server. Defaults to false.

section.para: Inspect or change the installation settings. The show subcommand generates a profile, a JSON document describing the current configuration. To change a configuration value, load a profile (complete or partial) using the load subcommand.
Generate an installation profile with the current settings. Settings without a value are not included in the output. The output can be used as input for agama config load.

listitem.para: Save the output here. Prints to standard output if not given.

section.para: Read and load a profile.

listitem.para: JSON file: URL or path, or - for standard input.

section.para: Validate a profile using JSON Schema. The schema is available at /usr/share/agama/schema/profile.schema.json. Validation is always performed as part of every other agama config command.

listitem.para: JSON file, URL or path, or - for standard input.
Run subcommands, if possible, in local mode, without trying to connect to a remote &agama; server. Defaults to false.

section.para: Generate and print a native &agama; JSON configuration from any supported profile kind and location. Supported kinds: JSON; Jsonnet (with hardware information injected); an &ay; profile, including ERB and rules/classes. Supported locations: a path, or a URL (including &ay;-specific schemes).

listitem.para: JSON file: URL or path, or - for standard input.

section.para: Edit and update an installation option using an external editor. Changes are discarded if the editor exits with an error code. If no editor is specified, the EDITOR environment variable is used, falling back to /usr/bin/vi as a last resort.

listitem.para: Editor command, including additional arguments if needed.

section.para: Analyze the system. In &agama; terminology, probing means analyzing the system: reading software repositories, analyzing storage devices, and more. This command starts that analysis and returns immediately.
Start the system installation.

warning.title: Destructive operation
warning.para: This command sets up the storage devices, installs packages, and so on. When the preconditions for installation are not met, it informs you and returns without making any changes to the system.

section.para: Handle installer questions. &agama; might require user intervention at any time; for example, it might ask you to supply missing information such as a password to decrypt a file system, or to decide what to do after an error such as a repository connection failure. This command answers such questions directly from the command line.
Set the mode for answering questions.

listitem.para: Ask the user and block the installation.
Do not block the installation.

section.para: Load predefined answers, to skip specific questions in interactive mode or change the answer in automatic mode.

listitem.para: Path to a file containing the answers in JSON format.

section.para: Print the list of questions waiting for an answer, in JSON format.
Read a question definition in JSON from standard input, and print the response once it is answered.

Collect the installer logs. The logs are stored in a compressed archive for further inspection, and include system and &agama;-specific logs and configuration files that are useful for troubleshooting and debugging.
Collect and store the logs in a tar archive.

listitem.para: Path to the destination directory and, optionally, the archive file name. The extension is added automatically.

section.para: List the logs to collect.

Authenticate with &agama;'s server. Unless you run this program as &rootuser;, you need to authenticate for most operations. Log in by specifying the &rootuser; password through agama auth login; on success, the server returns a JSON Web Token (JWT) that is stored and used to authenticate subsequent requests. If you run this program locally as &rootuser;, authentication is skipped automatically because it uses the master token at /run/agama/token (accessible only to &rootuser;).
Authenticate with &agama;'s server and store the token. Reads the password from standard input if available, otherwise prompts interactively. On success, the token is stored in .agama/agama-jwt.
Deauthenticate by removing the token. Does not affect &rootuser;.
Print the used token to standard output.

Download a file from a given &ay; URL. Useful for fetching additional scripts, configuration files, or &agama; auto-installation profiles using &ay;-supported schemes (for example, device://). To convert an &ay; profile instead, use agama config generate.

listitem.para: URL pointing to the file to download. A relative URL is resolved against the current working directory.
File name to save the download as.

section.para: Finish the installation.

listitem.para: What to do after finishing the installation:
stop: do not reboot. The &agama; backend keeps running.
halt: halt the installed machine.
poweroff: power off the installed machine.

section.para: Continuously monitor the &agama; service until it finishes.

When run from a terminal, agama monitor shows an interactive display and lets you answer a pending installer question directly, without preparing a separate answers file. This is the preferred way to answer a question that has already come up during installation; to answer a question before it is asked, predefine the answer in the profile's questions section instead (see ). When standard output is not a terminal, agama monitor falls back to plain text output.
Print the current state of the installation (for example, waiting, blocked, running, or finished).

listitem.para: The format to show the status in. Defaults to text.
json: machine-readable JSON format.
text: human-readable textual format that may be localized and is subject to change.

section.para: Display &agama; events.

listitem.para: Display the events in a more human-readable way.
